character_tex: Weyl-Kac characters at $z = 0$: $\chi_\lambda(q) = \eta(q)^{-\dim G}\sum_{\beta\in Q^\vee}\prod_{\alpha>0}\frac{(\alpha,\lambda+\rho+K\beta)}{(\alpha,\rho)}\,q^{|\lambda+\rho+K\beta|^2/2K}$, $K = k + h^\vee$, long roots of length$^2$ 2 (here $\dim G = 8$, $h^\vee = 3$, $K = 5$). One block per integrable highest weight, labelled by the $SU(3)$ irrep; $h_{\mathbf{1}} = 0$, $h_{\mathbf{3}} = \tfrac{4}{15}$, $h_{\bar{\mathbf{3}}} = \tfrac{4}{15}$, $h_{\mathbf{8}} = \tfrac{3}{5}$, $h_{\mathbf{6}} = \tfrac{2}{3}$, $h_{\bar{\mathbf{6}}} = \tfrac{2}{3}$.
description: Diagonal modular invariant of the $SU(3)$ WZW model at level 2, $c = k\dim G/(k+h^\vee) = \tfrac{16}{5}$. Characters from the Weyl-Kac formula specialised to $z=0$ (the finite Weyl sum becomes the Weyl dimension factor and the denominator becomes $\eta^{\dim G}$ by the Macdonald identity), summed exactly over the coroot lattice. The generator checks the Macdonald identity, the leading terms $\dim\lambda\, q^{h_\lambda-c/24}$ and that the weight-1 space of the vacuum module has dimension $\dim G = 8$, and compares with independent formulas: every product of two $SU(3)_1$ characters equals $\sum_c b^c_{ab}\chi^{SU(3)_2}_c$ with $b$ the 3-state Potts $\mathcal{W}_3$ (Rocha-Caridi) characters at $c = 4/5$ (the coset $SU(3)_1\times SU(3)_1/SU(3)_2$).
